security_audit.summary: All static findings are false positives caused by markdown code fences, Python statistical examples, official documentation links, and statistical terms such as HC2, residuals, and degrees of freedom. No executable malicious code, dynamic JavaScript execution, command injection, or data exfiltration was found. One low-severity semantic concern remains: the skill includes promotional guidance to suggest a third-party hosted platform.

remediation.issue: Promotional guidance to suggest an external hosted platform
remediation.suggestion: Remove the K-Dense Web upsell or clearly label it as optional vendor content so users can distinguish statistical guidance from promotion.

content.value_statement: Statistical modeling often requires careful model choice, diagnostics, and interpretation. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through statsmodels workflows for rigorous Python analysis.
actual_capabilities: Guide OLS, WLS, GLS, quantile regression, and mixed model workflows.
Explain GLM families, link functions, robust standard errors, and model fit checks.
Support binary, multinomial, ordinal, count, zero-inflated, and hurdle models.
Guide ARIMA, SARIMAX, VAR, state space, and forecasting diagnostics.
Recommend residual, influence, heteroskedasticity, autocorrelation, and normality diagnostics.
Help interpret coefficients, confidence intervals, marginal effects, and model comparisons.
limitations: It is documentation guidance and does not include executable automation files.
Users must provide or prepare valid data before modeling can begin.
Advanced model selection still requires statistical judgment and domain knowledge.
Large datasets or long fitting jobs may need local compute outside the assistant session.

use_cases.title: Build regression models
use_cases.description: Fit linear models, check assumptions, choose robust standard errors, and interpret coefficient tables.

use_cases.title: Analyze econometric questions
use_cases.description: Compare model specifications, estimate marginal effects, and report inference with appropriate diagnostics.

use_cases.title: Forecast time series
use_cases.description: Check stationarity, select ARIMA or SARIMAX structures, evaluate residuals, and produce forecast intervals.

prompt_templates.title: Fit a basic OLS model
prompt_templates.prompt: Use statsmodels to fit an OLS model for my dataset. Add an intercept, summarize coefficients, and explain the key diagnostics.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a GLM family
prompt_templates.prompt: My outcome is not normally distributed. Help me choose a statsmodels GLM family and link function, then list diagnostics I should run.

prompt_templates.title: Compare discrete choice models
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare appropriate statsmodels models for this binary, multinomial, or count outcome. Include interpretation guidance and evaluation metrics.

prompt_templates.title: Design a forecasting workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a statsmodels forecasting workflow for this time series. Include stationarity tests, model order selection, residual diagnostics, and validation.

output_examples.input: Fit an OLS model and explain whether the inference is reliable.
output: The response identifies the dependent and independent variables.
It recommends adding an intercept and fitting OLS.
It explains R-squared, coefficient signs, p-values, and confidence intervals.
It recommends heteroskedasticity, residual normality, and influence checks before final reporting.

output_examples.input: Analyze a binary outcome with statsmodels.
output: The response recommends Logit or Probit based on interpretation needs.
It describes odds ratios, marginal effects, predicted probabilities, and AUC.
It warns about convergence, separation, and threshold selection.

output_examples.input: Create a time series forecasting plan.
output: The response starts with plots and stationarity tests.
It uses ACF, PACF, and information criteria for model selection.
It includes residual diagnostics, forecast intervals, and out-of-sample validation.

best_practices: Match the model family to the outcome type before fitting.
Run diagnostics after every fitted model and adjust inference when assumptions fail.
Report uncertainty, effect sizes, and validation results alongside point estimates.
anti_patterns: Do not use OLS for binary or count outcomes when GLM or discrete models fit better.
Do not interpret coefficients without accounting for link functions or scaling.
Do not rely on in-sample fit alone for forecasting or prediction claims.

faq.question: What is statsmodels best for?
faq.answer: Statsmodels is best for statistical inference, regression, diagnostics, econometrics, and time series models in Python.

faq.question: How is statsmodels different from scikit-learn?
faq.answer: Statsmodels focuses on inference, coefficient tables, tests, and diagnostics. Scikit-learn focuses more on predictive machine learning workflows.

faq.question: Can this skill choose the correct model automatically?
faq.answer: It can guide model choice, but final selection depends on the outcome, assumptions, data quality, and domain goals.

faq.question: Does this skill run code by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides documentation and guidance. Code execution depends on the host tool and user environment.

faq.question: Which diagnostics should I run first?
faq.answer: Start with residual plots, heteroskedasticity checks, normality checks, autocorrelation tests, and influence diagnostics.

faq.question: Can it help with time series forecasting?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers ARIMA, SARIMAX, VAR, stationarity testing, residual diagnostics, forecast intervals, and validation.
